issue.description: Review only ADR-023 section 2.2 and research/specs/secret-ruleset-v4.md sections 2.2 and 4.4. Check the randomness qualifier P/Q truth table, deterministic word-run and m semantics, excluded identifiers, bead-ID shape, credential-assignment forms, table-row delimiters, and value-span rules against the accepted secret-rejection-v1 and synthetic fixtures. Stay within the clean-room sources and do not derive implementation from another tool. Acceptance: record in this bead's notes a scoped pass or actionable rejection naming the checked sections and fixture evidence, and explicitly state whether these inputs are deterministic enough for compatible implementations.
issue.notes:
Scoped outcome: ACTIONABLE REJECTION. No source or test files changed; no source commit is warranted.

Scope and evidence: ADR-023 has no numbered section 2.2; I checked its randomness rationale in Decision item 5 (ADR-023 SHA-256 39d9174173df3aadc7c268bdd27d139e1091cc12559e20b9d098037683a7359a). Checked research/specs/secret-ruleset-v4.md section 2.2 (section SHA-256 84fb12e9d02a1ad9055c40252e2fe062ddba73d73281969a742b0752eff6f0e7) and section 4.4 (section SHA-256 530c1564d7cecfa3624550ff71c668140c4cd00bbedd62cf92bcabd0a027d284), against accepted research/specs/secret-rejection-v1.md (SHA-256 f6aa7639a8ef1dd509b431853abf64db78d0923ef9e9d59b09e0a4e0e55df231). The ruleset file at local HEAD has SHA-256 bad7c8102086d8128465e284b839673ceceb84b28e3ea7bf55835dfaee5ad5a9; origin/main is one commit ahead with an unrelated section 4.3 edit, and the reviewed sections are unchanged.

Fixture evidence: research/fixtures has no secret-ruleset-v4 truth-table or credential-assignment fixture set. Its only secret-related artifact, secret-write-boundary-v1.json, covers mutation surfaces and has no Q classes, excluded-identifier cases, expected verdicts, or byte spans. Ruleset section 7 requires runtime synthetic truth-table fixtures but publishes no rows or results, so the required fixture comparisons are not independently reproducible from the clean-room fixture artifacts.

Findings: the integer gates in section 2.2 are deterministic once the parsed value and w are fixed, but the scan does not define whether a four-or-more letter match consumes the maximal run or how far the cursor advances. The formula a-w>=m gives an absolute count of alphanumeric bytes outside the matched word runs, but the prose “non-word material” could imply punctuation contributes; the required truth-table rows are absent to confirm intent. Section 2.2 says a bead identifier fails but supplies no bead-ID shape or truth-table row. In section 4.4, identifier components and lower-to-upper boundaries lack an explicit byte/tokenization rule. Form 1 operators overlap (`:` with `:=`, `=` with `=>`) without precedence. Form 2 does not define the count/class of “spaces.” Form 3 does not define spacing around a pipe delimiter or whether a terminal pipe is syntax or part of the maximal value run; since `|` is allowed by the value character rule but makes P true, this changes the verdict and reported span. The value rule also leaves the exact quote bytes and repeated trailing-punctuation trimming unspecified. The listed exclusions can be identified, but the missing table provides no positive/negative fixture row for each one.

The v1 contract requires deterministic offline findings and byte ranges; its statistical/entropy advisory rule does not by itself contradict the context-bound Q rule, which ADR-023 explicitly says is not an entropy threshold. However, the missing parser and fixture semantics prevent independently compatible implementations from reliably reaching the same verdicts and spans.

Conclusion: these inputs are NOT deterministic enough for compatible implementations. Resolve by publishing the synthetic Q/exclusion truth table with expected verdicts and byte spans, defining maximal word-run consumption and confirming m's formula against its prose, identifier tokenization and bead-ID shape, form delimiter/whitespace precedence, and exact value/quote/trimming boundaries.
issue.title: Review randomness and identifier truth-table semantics for BR-T35
